text: “Oh, I have. There are a great many Nihilists about nowadays, you know, and indeed it is not to be wondered at. What sort of days are they? I ask you. But we thought... you are not a Nihilist of course? Answer me openly, openly!”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Believe me, you can speak openly to me as you would to yourself! Official duty is one thing but... you are thinking I meant to say friendship is quite another? No, you’re wrong! It’s not friendship, but the feeling of a man and a citizen, the feeling of humanity and of love for the Almighty. I may be an official, but I am always bound to feel myself a man and a citizen.... You were asking about Zametov. Zametov will make a scandal in the French style in a house of bad reputation, over a glass of champagne... that’s all your Zametov is good for! While I’m perhaps, so to speak, burning with devotion and lofty feelings, and besides I have rank, consequence, a post! I am married and have children, I fulfil the duties of a man and a citizen, but who is he, may I ask? I appeal to you as a man ennobled by education... Then these midwives, too, have become extraordinarily numerous.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov raised his eyebrows inquiringly.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The words of Ilya Petrovitch, who had obviously been dining, were for the most part a stream of empty sounds for him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But some of them he understood.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He looked at him inquiringly, not knowing how it would end.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “I mean those crop-headed wenches,” the talkative Ilya Petrovitch continued.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Midwives is my name for them. I think it a very satisfactory one, ha-ha! They go to the Academy, study anatomy. If I fall ill, am I to send for a young lady to treat me? What do you say? Ha-ha! Ilya Petrovitch laughed, quite pleased with his own wit. “It’s an immoderate zeal for education, but once you’re educated, that’s enough. Why abuse it? Why insult honourable people, as that scoundrel Zametov does? Why did he insult me, I ask you? Look at these suicides, too, how common they are, you can’t fancy! People spend their last halfpenny and kill themselves, boys and girls and old people. Only this morning we heard about a gentleman who had just come to town. Nil Pavlitch, I say, what was the name of that gentleman who shot himself?”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Svidrigaïlov,” someone answered from the other room with drowsy listlessness.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov started.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Svidrigaïlov! Svidrigaïlov has shot himself!” he cried.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “What, do you know Svidrigaïlov?”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Yes... I knew him.... He hadn’t been here long.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Yes, that’s so. He had lost his wife, was a man of reckless habits and all of a sudden shot himself, and in such a shocking way.... He left in his notebook a few words: that he dies in full possession of his faculties and that no one is to blame for his death. He had money, they say. How did you come to know him?”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “I... was acquainted... my sister was governess in his family.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Bah-bah-bah! Then no doubt you can tell us something about him. You had no suspicion?”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “I saw him yesterday... he... was drinking wine; I knew nothing.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov felt as though something had fallen on him and was stifling him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “You’ve turned pale again. It’s so stuffy here...”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Yes, I must go,” muttered Raskolnikov.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Excuse my troubling you....”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Oh, not at all, as often as you like. It’s a pleasure to see you and I am glad to say so.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Ilya Petrovitch held out his hand.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “I only wanted... I came to see Zametov.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “I understand, I understand, and it’s a pleasure to see you.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “I... am very glad... good-bye,” Raskolnikov smiled.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He went out; he reeled, he was overtaken with giddiness and did not know what he was doing.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He began going down the stairs, supporting himself with his right hand against the wall.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He fancied that a porter pushed past him on his way upstairs to the police office, that a dog in the lower storey kept up a shrill barking and that a woman flung a rolling-pin at it and shouted.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He went down and out into the yard.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There, not far from the entrance, stood Sonia, pale and horror-stricken.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She looked wildly at him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He stood still before her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There was a look of poignant agony, of despair, in her face.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She clasped her hands.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: His lips worked in an ugly, meaningless smile.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He stood still a minute, grinned and went back to the police office.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Ilya Petrovitch had sat down and was rummaging among some papers.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Before him stood the same peasant who had pushed by on the stairs.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Hulloa! Back again! have you left something behind? What’s the matter?”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov, with white lips and staring eyes, came slowly nearer.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He walked right to the table, leaned his hand on it, tried to say something, but could not; only incoherent sounds were audible.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “You are feeling ill, a chair! Here, sit down! Some water!”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov dropped on to a chair, but he kept his eyes fixed on the face of Ilya Petrovitch, which expressed unpleasant surprise.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Both looked at one another for a minute and waited.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Water was brought.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “It was I...” began Raskolnikov.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Drink some water.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov refused the water with his hand, and softly and brokenly, but distinctly said:

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “It was I killed the old pawnbroker woman and her sister Lizaveta with an axe and robbed them.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Ilya Petrovitch opened his mouth.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: People ran up on all sides.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov repeated his statement.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Siberia.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: On the banks of a broad solitary river stands a town, one of the administrative centres of Russia; in the town there is a fortress, in the fortress there is a prison.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: In the prison the second-class convict Rodion Raskolnikov has been confined for nine months.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Almost a year and a half has passed since his crime.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There had been little difficulty about his trial.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The criminal adhered exactly, firmly, and clearly to his statement.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He did not confuse nor misrepresent the facts, nor soften them in his own interest, nor omit the smallest detail.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He explained every incident of the murder, the secret of the pledge (the piece of wood with a strip of metal) which was found in the murdered woman’s hand.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He described minutely how he had taken her keys, what they were like, as well as the chest and its contents; he explained the mystery of Lizaveta’s murder; described how Koch and, after him, the student knocked, and repeated all they had said to one another; how he afterwards had run downstairs and heard Nikolay and Dmitri shouting; how he had hidden in the empty flat and afterwards gone home.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He ended by indicating the stone in the yard off the Voznesensky Prospect under which the purse and the trinkets were found.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The whole thing, in fact, was perfectly clear.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The lawyers and the judges were very much struck, among other things, by the fact that he had hidden the trinkets and the purse under a stone, without making use of them, and that, what was more, he did not now remember what the trinkets were like, or even how many there were.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The fact that he had never opened the purse and did not even know how much was in it seemed incredible.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There turned out to be in the purse three hundred and seventeen roubles and sixty copecks.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: From being so long under the stone, some of the most valuable notes lying uppermost had suffered from the damp.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They were a long while trying to discover why the accused man should tell a lie about this, when about everything else he had made a truthful and straightforward confession.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Finally some of the lawyers more versed in psychology admitted that it was possible he had really not looked into the purse, and so didn’t know what was in it when he hid it under the stone.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But they immediately drew the deduction that the crime could only have been committed through temporary mental derangement, through homicidal mania, without object or the pursuit of gain.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: This fell in with the most recent fashionable theory of temporary insanity, so often applied in our days in criminal cases.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Moreover Raskolnikov’s hypochondriacal condition was proved by many witnesses, by Dr. Zossimov, his former fellow students, his landlady and her servant.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: All this pointed strongly to the conclusion that Raskolnikov was not quite like an ordinary murderer and robber, but that there was another element in the case.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: To the intense annoyance of those who maintained this opinion, the criminal scarcely attempted to defend himself.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: To the decisive question as to what motive impelled him to the murder and the robbery, he answered very clearly with the coarsest frankness that the cause was his miserable position, his poverty and helplessness, and his desire to provide for his first steps in life by the help of the three thousand roubles he had reckoned on finding.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He had been led to the murder through his shallow and cowardly nature, exasperated moreover by privation and failure.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: To the question what led him to confess, he answered that it was his heartfelt repentance.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: All this was almost coarse....

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The sentence however was more merciful than could have been expected, perhaps partly because the criminal had not tried to justify himself, but had rather shown a desire to exaggerate his guilt.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: All the strange and peculiar circumstances of the crime were taken into consideration.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There could be no doubt of the abnormal and poverty-stricken condition of the criminal at the time.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The fact that he had made no use of what he had stolen was put down partly to the effect of remorse, partly to his abnormal mental condition at the time of the crime.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Incidentally the murder of Lizaveta served indeed to confirm the last hypothesis: a man commits two murders and forgets that the door is open!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Finally, the confession, at the very moment when the case was hopelessly muddled by the false evidence given by Nikolay through melancholy and fanaticism, and when, moreover, there were no proofs against the real criminal, no suspicions even (Porfiry Petrovitch fully kept his word)--all this did much to soften the sentence.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Other circumstances, too, in the prisoner’s favour came out quite unexpectedly.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Razumihin somehow discovered and proved that while Raskolnikov was at the university he had helped a poor consumptive fellow student and had spent his last penny on supporting him for six months, and when this student died, leaving a decrepit old father whom he had maintained almost from his thirteenth year, Raskolnikov had got the old man into a hospital and paid for his funeral when he died.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov’s landlady bore witness, too, that when they had lived in another house at Five Corners, Raskolnikov had rescued two little children from a house on fire and was burnt in doing so.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: This was investigated and fairly well confirmed by many witnesses.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: These facts made an impression in his favour.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: And in the end the criminal was, in consideration of extenuating circumstances, condemned to penal servitude in the second class for a term of eight years only.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At the very beginning of the trial Raskolnikov’s mother fell ill.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Dounia and Razumihin found it possible to get her out of Petersburg during the trial.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Razumihin chose a town on the railway not far from Petersburg, so as to be able to follow every step of the trial and at the same time to see Avdotya Romanovna as often as possible.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Pulcheria Alexandrovna’s illness was a strange nervous one and was accompanied by a partial derangement of her intellect.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: When Dounia returned from her last interview with her brother, she had found her mother already ill, in feverish delirium.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: That evening Razumihin and she agreed what answers they must make to her mother’s questions about Raskolnikov and made up a complete story for her mother’s benefit of his having to go away to a distant part of Russia on a business commission, which would bring him in the end money and reputation.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But they were struck by the fact that Pulcheria Alexandrovna never asked them anything on the subject, neither then nor thereafter.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: On the contrary, she had her own version of her son’s sudden departure; she told them with tears how he had come to say good-bye to her, hinting that she alone knew many mysterious and important facts, and that Rodya had many very powerful enemies, so that it was necessary for him to be in hiding.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: As for his future career, she had no doubt that it would be brilliant when certain sinister influences could be removed.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She assured Razumihin that her son would be one day a great statesman, that his article and brilliant literary talent proved it.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: This article she was continually reading, she even read it aloud, almost took it to bed with her, but scarcely asked where Rodya was, though the subject was obviously avoided by the others, which might have been enough to awaken her suspicions.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They began to be frightened at last at Pulcheria Alexandrovna’s strange silence on certain subjects.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She did not, for instance, complain of getting no letters from him, though in previous years she had only lived on the hope of letters from her beloved Rodya.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: This was the cause of great uneasiness to Dounia; the idea occurred to her that her mother suspected that there was something terrible in her son’s fate and was afraid to ask, for fear of hearing something still more awful.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: In any case, Dounia saw clearly that her mother was not in full possession of her faculties.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: It happened once or twice, however, that Pulcheria Alexandrovna gave such a turn to the conversation that it was impossible to answer her without mentioning where Rodya was, and on receiving unsatisfactory and suspicious answers she became at once gloomy and silent, and this mood lasted for a long time.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Dounia saw at last that it was hard to deceive her and came to the conclusion that it was better to be absolutely silent on certain points; but it became more and more evident that the poor mother suspected something terrible.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Dounia remembered her brother’s telling her that her mother had overheard her talking in her sleep on the night after her interview with Svidrigaïlov and before the fatal day of the confession: had not she made out something from that?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Sometimes days and even weeks of gloomy silence and tears would be succeeded by a period of hysterical animation, and the invalid would begin to talk almost incessantly of her son, of her hopes of his future....

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Her fancies were sometimes very strange.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They humoured her, pretended to agree with her (she saw perhaps that they were pretending), but she still went on talking.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Five months after Raskolnikov’s confession, he was sentenced.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Razumihin and Sonia saw him in prison as often as it was possible.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At last the moment of separation came.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Dounia swore to her brother that the separation should not be for ever, Razumihin did the same.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Razumihin, in his youthful ardour, had firmly resolved to lay the foundations at least of a secure livelihood during the next three or four years, and saving up a certain sum, to emigrate to Siberia, a country rich in every natural resource and in need of workers, active men and capital.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There they would settle in the town where Rodya was and all together would begin a new life.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They all wept at parting.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov had been very dreamy for a few days before.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He asked a great deal about his mother and was constantly anxious about her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He worried so much about her that it alarmed Dounia.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: When he heard about his mother’s illness he became very gloomy.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: With Sonia he was particularly reserved all the time.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: With the help of the money left to her by Svidrigaïlov, Sonia had long ago made her preparations to follow the party of convicts in which he was despatched to Siberia.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Not a word passed between Raskolnikov and her on the subject, but both knew it would be so.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At the final leave-taking he smiled strangely at his sister’s and Razumihin’s fervent anticipations of their happy future together when he should come out of prison.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He predicted that their mother’s illness would soon have a fatal ending.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Sonia and he at last set off.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Two months later Dounia was married to Razumihin.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: It was a quiet and sorrowful wedding; Porfiry Petrovitch and Zossimov were invited however.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: During all this period Razumihin wore an air of resolute determination.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Dounia put implicit faith in his carrying out his plans and indeed she could not but believe in him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He displayed a rare strength of will.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Among other things he began attending university lectures again in order to take his degree.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They were continually making plans for the future; both counted on settling in Siberia within five years at least.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Till then they rested their hopes on Sonia.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Pulcheria Alexandrovna was delighted to give her blessing to Dounia’s marriage with Razumihin; but after the marriage she became even more melancholy and anxious.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: To give her pleasure Razumihin told her how Raskolnikov had looked after the poor student and his decrepit father and how a year ago he had been burnt and injured in rescuing two little children from a fire.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: These two pieces of news excited Pulcheria Alexandrovna’s disordered imagination almost to ecstasy.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She was continually talking about them, even entering into conversation with strangers in the street, though Dounia always accompanied her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: In public conveyances and shops, wherever she could capture a listener, she would begin to discourse about her son, his article, how he had helped the student, how he had been burnt at the fire, and so on!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Dounia did not know how to restrain her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Apart from the danger of her morbid excitement, there was the risk of someone’s recalling Raskolnikov’s name and speaking of the recent trial.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Pulcheria Alexandrovna found out the address of the mother of the two children her son had saved and insisted on going to see her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At last her restlessness reached an extreme point.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She would sometimes begin to cry suddenly and was often ill and feverishly delirious.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: One morning she declared that by her reckoning Rodya ought soon to be home, that she remembered when he said good-bye to her he said that they must expect him back in nine months.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She began to prepare for his coming, began to do up her room for him, to clean the furniture, to wash and put up new hangings and so on.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Dounia was anxious, but said nothing and helped her to arrange the room.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: After a fatiguing day spent in continual fancies, in joyful day-dreams and tears, Pulcheria Alexandrovna was taken ill in the night and by morning she was feverish and delirious.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: It was brain fever.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She died within a fortnight.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: In her delirium she dropped words which showed that she knew a great deal more about her son’s terrible fate than they had supposed.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: For a long time Raskolnikov did not know of his mother’s death, though a regular correspondence had been maintained from the time he reached Siberia.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: It was carried on by means of Sonia, who wrote every month to the Razumihins and received an answer with unfailing regularity.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At first they found Sonia’s letters dry and unsatisfactory, but later on they came to the conclusion that the letters could not be better, for from these letters they received a complete picture of their unfortunate brother’s life.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Sonia’s letters were full of the most matter-of-fact detail, the simplest and clearest description of all Raskolnikov’s surroundings as a convict.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There was no word of her own hopes, no conjecture as to the future, no description of her feelings.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Instead of any attempt to interpret his state of mind and inner life, she gave the simple facts--that is, his own words, an exact account of his health, what he asked for at their interviews, what commission he gave her and so on.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: All these facts she gave with extraordinary minuteness.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The picture of their unhappy brother stood out at last with great clearness and precision.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There could be no mistake, because nothing was given but facts.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But Dounia and her husband could get little comfort out of the news, especially at first.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Sonia wrote that he was constantly sullen and not ready to talk, that he scarcely seemed interested in the news she gave him from their letters, that he sometimes asked after his mother and that when, seeing that he had guessed the truth, she told him at last of her death, she was surprised to find that he did not seem greatly affected by it, not externally at any rate.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She told them that, although he seemed so wrapped up in himself and, as it were, shut himself off from everyone--he took a very direct and simple view of his new life; that he understood his position, expected nothing better for the time, had no ill-founded hopes (as is so common in his position) and scarcely seemed surprised at anything in his surroundings, so unlike anything he had known before.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She wrote that his health was satisfactory; he did his work without shirking or seeking to do more; he was almost indifferent about food, but except on Sundays and holidays the food was so bad that at last he had been glad to accept some money from her, Sonia, to have his own tea every day.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He begged her not to trouble about anything else, declaring that all this fuss about him only annoyed him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Sonia wrote further that in prison he shared the same room with the rest, that she had not seen the inside of their barracks, but concluded that they were crowded, miserable and unhealthy; that he slept on a plank bed with a rug under him and was unwilling to make any other arrangement.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But that he lived so poorly and roughly, not from any plan or design, but simply from inattention and indifference.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Sonia wrote simply that he had at first shown no interest in her visits, had almost been vexed with her indeed for coming, unwilling to talk and rude to her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But that in the end these visits had become a habit and almost a necessity for him, so that he was positively distressed when she was ill for some days and could not visit him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She used to see him on holidays at the prison gates or in the guard-room, to which he was brought for a few minutes to see her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: On working days she would go to see him at work either at the workshops or at the brick kilns, or at the sheds on the banks of the Irtish.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: About herself, Sonia wrote that she had succeeded in making some acquaintances in the town, that she did sewing, and, as there was scarcely a dressmaker in the town, she was looked upon as an indispensable person in many houses.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But she did not mention that the authorities were, through her, interested in Raskolnikov; that his task was lightened and so on.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At last the news came (Dounia had indeed noticed signs of alarm and uneasiness in the preceding letters) that he held aloof from everyone, that his fellow prisoners did not like him, that he kept silent for days at a time and was becoming very pale.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: In the last letter Sonia wrote that he had been taken very seriously ill and was in the convict ward of the hospital.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He was ill a long time.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But it was not the horrors of prison life, not the hard labour, the bad food, the shaven head, or the patched clothes that crushed him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: What did he care for all those trials and hardships! he was even glad of the hard work.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Physically exhausted, he could at least reckon on a few hours of quiet sleep.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: And what was the food to him--the thin cabbage soup with beetles floating in it?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: In the past as a student he had often not had even that.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: His clothes were warm and suited to his manner of life.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He did not even feel the fetters.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Was he ashamed of his shaven head and parti-coloured coat?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Before whom?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Before Sonia?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Sonia was afraid of him, how could he be ashamed before her?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: And yet he was ashamed even before Sonia, whom he tortured because of it with his contemptuous rough manner.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But it was not his shaven head and his fetters he was ashamed of: his pride had been stung to the quick.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: It was wounded pride that made him ill.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Oh, how happy he would have been if he could have blamed himself!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He could have borne anything then, even shame and disgrace.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But he judged himself severely, and his exasperated conscience found no particularly terrible fault in his past, except a simple blunder which might happen to anyone.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He was ashamed just because he, Raskolnikov, had so hopelessly, stupidly come to grief through some decree of blind fate, and must humble himself and submit to “the idiocy” of a sentence, if he were anyhow to be at peace.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Vague and objectless anxiety in the present, and in the future a continual sacrifice leading to nothing--that was all that lay before him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: And what comfort was it to him that at the end of eight years he would only be thirty-two and able to begin a new life!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: What had he to live for?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: What had he to look forward to?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Why should he strive?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: To live in order to exist?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Why, he had been ready a thousand times before to give up existence for the sake of an idea, for a hope, even for a fancy.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Mere existence had always been too little for him; he had always wanted more.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Perhaps it was just because of the strength of his desires that he had thought himself a man to whom more was permissible than to others.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: And if only fate would have sent him repentance--burning repentance that would have torn his heart and robbed him of sleep, that repentance, the awful agony of which brings visions of hanging or drowning!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Oh, he would have been glad of it!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Tears and agonies would at least have been life.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But he did not repent of his crime.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At least he might have found relief in raging at his stupidity, as he had raged at the grotesque blunders that had brought him to prison.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But now in prison, in freedom, he thought over and criticised all his actions again and by no means found them so blundering and so grotesque as they had seemed at the fatal time.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “In what way,” he asked himself, “was my theory stupider than others that have swarmed and clashed from the beginning of the world? One has only to look at the thing quite independently, broadly, and uninfluenced by commonplace ideas, and my idea will by no means seem so... strange. Oh, sceptics and halfpenny philosophers, why do you halt half-way!”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Why does my action strike them as so horrible?” he said to himself.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Is it because it was a crime? What is meant by crime? My conscience is at rest. Of course, it was a legal crime, of course, the letter of the law was broken and blood was shed. Well, punish me for the letter of the law... and that’s enough. Of course, in that case many of the benefactors of mankind who snatched power for themselves instead of inheriting it ought to have been punished at their first steps. But those men succeeded and so they were right, and I didn’t, and so I had no right to have taken that step.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: It was only in that that he recognised his criminality, only in the fact that he had been unsuccessful and had confessed it.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He suffered too from the question: why had he not killed himself?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Why had he stood looking at the river and preferred to confess?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Was the desire to live so strong and was it so hard to overcome it?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Had not Svidrigaïlov overcome it, although he was afraid of death?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: In misery he asked himself this question, and could not understand that, at the very time he had been standing looking into the river, he had perhaps been dimly conscious of the fundamental falsity in himself and his convictions.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He didn’t understand that that consciousness might be the promise of a future crisis, of a new view of life and of his future resurrection.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He preferred to attribute it to the dead weight of instinct which he could not step over, again through weakness and meanness.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He looked at his fellow prisoners and was amazed to see how they all loved life and prized it.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: It seemed to him that they loved and valued life more in prison than in freedom.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: What terrible agonies and privations some of them, the tramps for instance, had endured!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Could they care so much for a ray of sunshine, for the primeval forest, the cold spring hidden away in some unseen spot, which the tramp had marked three years before, and longed to see again, as he might to see his sweetheart, dreaming of the green grass round it and the bird singing in the bush?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: As he went on he saw still more inexplicable examples.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: In prison, of course, there was a great deal he did not see and did not want to see; he lived as it were with downcast eyes.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: It was loathsome and unbearable for him to look.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But in the end there was much that surprised him and he began, as it were involuntarily, to notice much that he had not suspected before.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: What surprised him most of all was the terrible impossible gulf that lay between him and all the rest.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They seemed to be a different species, and he looked at them and they at him with distrust and hostility.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He felt and knew the reasons of his isolation, but he would never have admitted till then that those reasons were so deep and strong.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There were some Polish exiles, political prisoners, among them.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They simply looked down upon all the rest as ignorant churls; but Raskolnikov could not look upon them like that.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He saw that these ignorant men were in many respects far wiser than the Poles.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There were some Russians who were just as contemptuous, a former officer and two seminarists.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov saw their mistake as clearly.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He was disliked and avoided by everyone; they even began to hate him at last--why, he could not tell.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Men who had been far more guilty despised and laughed at his crime.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “You’re a gentleman,” they used to say.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “You shouldn’t hack about with an axe; that’s not a gentleman’s work.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The second week in Lent, his turn came to take the sacrament with his gang.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He went to church and prayed with the others.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: A quarrel broke out one day, he did not know how.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: All fell on him at once in a fury.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “You’re an infidel! You don’t believe in God,” they shouted.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “You ought to be killed.”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He had never talked to them about God nor his belief, but they wanted to kill him as an infidel.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He said nothing.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: One of the prisoners rushed at him in a perfect frenzy.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov awaited him calmly and silently; his eyebrows did not quiver, his face did not flinch.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The guard succeeded in intervening between him and his assailant, or there would have been bloodshed.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There was another question he could not decide: why were they all so fond of Sonia?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She did not try to win their favour; she rarely met them, sometimes only she came to see him at work for a moment.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: And yet everybody knew her, they knew that she had come out to follow him, knew how and where she lived.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She never gave them money, did them no particular services.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Only once at Christmas she sent them all presents of pies and rolls.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But by degrees closer relations sprang up between them and Sonia.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She would write and post letters for them to their relations.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Relations of the prisoners who visited the town, at their instructions, left with Sonia presents and money for them.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Their wives and sweethearts knew her and used to visit her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: And when she visited Raskolnikov at work, or met a party of the prisoners on the road, they all took off their hats to her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: “Little mother Sofya Semyonovna, you are our dear, good little mother,” coarse branded criminals said to that frail little creature.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She would smile and bow to them and everyone was delighted when she smiled.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They even admired her gait and turned round to watch her walking; they admired her too for being so little, and, in fact, did not know what to admire her most for.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They even came to her for help in their illnesses.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He was in the hospital from the middle of Lent till after Easter.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: When he was better, he remembered the dreams he had had while he was feverish and delirious.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He dreamt that the whole world was condemned to a terrible new strange plague that had come to Europe from the depths of Asia.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: All were to be destroyed except a very few chosen.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Some new sorts of microbes were attacking the bodies of men, but these microbes were endowed with intelligence and will.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Men attacked by them became at once mad and furious.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But never had men considered themselves so intellectual and so completely in possession of the truth as these sufferers, never had they considered their decisions, their scientific conclusions, their moral convictions so infallible.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Whole villages, whole towns and peoples went mad from the infection.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: All were excited and did not understand one another.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Each thought that he alone had the truth and was wretched looking at the others, beat himself on the breast, wept, and wrung his hands.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They did not know how to judge and could not agree what to consider evil and what good; they did not know whom to blame, whom to justify.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Men killed each other in a sort of senseless spite.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They gathered together in armies against one another, but even on the march the armies would begin attacking each other, the ranks would be broken and the soldiers would fall on each other, stabbing and cutting, biting and devouring each other.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The alarm bell was ringing all day long in the towns; men rushed together, but why they were summoned and who was summoning them no one knew.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The most ordinary trades were abandoned, because everyone proposed his own ideas, his own improvements, and they could not agree.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The land too was abandoned.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Men met in groups, agreed on something, swore to keep together, but at once began on something quite different from what they had proposed.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They accused one another, fought and killed each other.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There were conflagrations and famine.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: All men and all things were involved in destruction.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The plague spread and moved further and further.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Only a few men could be saved in the whole world.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They were a pure chosen people, destined to found a new race and a new life, to renew and purify the earth, but no one had seen these men, no one had heard their words and their voices.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov was worried that this senseless dream haunted his memory so miserably, the impression of this feverish delirium persisted so long.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The second week after Easter had come.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There were warm bright spring days; in the prison ward the grating windows under which the sentinel paced were opened.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Sonia had only been able to visit him twice during his illness; each time she had to obtain permission, and it was difficult.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But she often used to come to the hospital yard, especially in the evening, sometimes only to stand a minute and look up at the windows of the ward.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: One evening, when he was almost well again, Raskolnikov fell asleep.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: On waking up he chanced to go to the window, and at once saw Sonia in the distance at the hospital gate.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She seemed to be waiting for someone.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Something stabbed him to the heart at that minute.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He shuddered and moved away from the window.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Next day Sonia did not come, nor the day after; he noticed that he was expecting her uneasily.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At last he was discharged.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: On reaching the prison he learnt from the convicts that Sofya Semyonovna was lying ill at home and was unable to go out.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He was very uneasy and sent to inquire after her; he soon learnt that her illness was not dangerous.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Hearing that he was anxious about her, Sonia sent him a pencilled note, telling him that she was much better, that she had a slight cold and that she would soon, very soon come and see him at his work.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: His heart throbbed painfully as he read it.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Again it was a warm bright day.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Early in the morning, at six o’clock, he went off to work on the river bank, where they used to pound alabaster and where there was a kiln for baking it in a shed.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There were only three of them sent.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: One of the convicts went with the guard to the fortress to fetch a tool; the other began getting the wood ready and laying it in the kiln.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov came out of the shed on to the river bank, sat down on a heap of logs by the shed and began gazing at the wide deserted river.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: From the high bank a broad landscape opened before him, the sound of singing floated faintly audible from the other bank.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: In the vast steppe, bathed in sunshine, he could just see, like black specks, the nomads’ tents.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: There there was freedom, there other men were living, utterly unlike those here; there time itself seemed to stand still, as though the age of Abraham and his flocks had not passed.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Raskolnikov sat gazing, his thoughts passed into day-dreams, into contemplation; he thought of nothing, but a vague restlessness excited and troubled him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Suddenly he found Sonia beside him; she had come up noiselessly and sat down at his side.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: It was still quite early; the morning chill was still keen.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She wore her poor old burnous and the green shawl; her face still showed signs of illness, it was thinner and paler.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She gave him a joyful smile of welcome, but held out her hand with her usual timidity.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She was always timid of holding out her hand to him and sometimes did not offer it at all, as though afraid he would repel it.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He always took her hand as though with repugnance, always seemed vexed to meet her and was sometimes obstinately silent throughout her visit.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Sometimes she trembled before him and went away deeply grieved.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But now their hands did not part.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He stole a rapid glance at her and dropped his eyes on the ground without speaking.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They were alone, no one had seen them.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The guard had turned away for the time.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: How it happened he did not know.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But all at once something seemed to seize him and fling him at her feet.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He wept and threw his arms round her knees.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: For the first instant she was terribly frightened and she turned pale.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She jumped up and looked at him trembling.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But at the same moment she understood, and a light of infinite happiness came into her eyes.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She knew and had no doubt that he loved her beyond everything and that at last the moment had come....

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They wanted to speak, but could not; tears stood in their eyes.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They were both pale and thin; but those sick pale faces were bright with the dawn of a new future, of a full resurrection into a new life.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They were renewed by love; the heart of each held infinite sources of life for the heart of the other.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They resolved to wait and be patient.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: They had another seven years to wait, and what terrible suffering and what infinite happiness before them!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But he had risen again and he knew it and felt it in all his being, while she--she only lived in his life.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: On the evening of the same day, when the barracks were locked, Raskolnikov lay on his plank bed and thought of her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He had even fancied that day that all the convicts who had been his enemies looked at him differently; he had even entered into talk with them and they answered him in a friendly way.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He remembered that now, and thought it was bound to be so.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Wasn’t everything now bound to be changed?

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He thought of her.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He remembered how continually he had tormented her and wounded her heart.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He remembered her pale and thin little face.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But these recollections scarcely troubled him now; he knew with what infinite love he would now repay all her sufferings.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: And what were all, all the agonies of the past!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Everything, even his crime, his sentence and imprisonment, seemed to him now in the first rush of feeling an external, strange fact with which he had no concern.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But he could not think for long together of anything that evening, and he could not have analysed anything consciously; he was simply feeling.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Life had stepped into the place of theory and something quite different would work itself out in his mind.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Under his pillow lay the New Testament.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He took it up mechanically.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: The book belonged to Sonia; it was the one from which she had read the raising of Lazarus to him.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At first he was afraid that she would worry him about religion, would talk about the gospel and pester him with books.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But to his great surprise she had not once approached the subject and had not even offered him the Testament.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He had asked her for it himself not long before his illness and she brought him the book without a word.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Till now he had not opened it.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He did not open it now, but one thought passed through his mind: “Can her convictions not be mine now? Her feelings, her aspirations at least....”

title: Crime and Punishment
text: She too had been greatly agitated that day, and at night she was taken ill again.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But she was so happy--and so unexpectedly happy--that she was almost frightened of her happiness.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: Seven years, only seven years!

title: Crime and Punishment
text: At the beginning of their happiness at some moments they were both ready to look on those seven years as though they were seven days.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: He did not know that the new life would not be given him for nothing, that he would have to pay dearly for it, that it would cost him great striving, great suffering.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: But that is the beginning of a new story--the story of the gradual renewal of a man, the story of his gradual regeneration, of his passing from one world into another, of his initiation into a new unknown life.

title: Crime and Punishment
text: That might be the subject of a new story, but our present story is ended.
